concept.name: Volume confirmation
concept.definition: The use of expanding volume to validate a price move: breakouts, trend legs, and reversals are considered more credible when accompanied by above-average participation. Within Wyckoff logic, confirmation is effort (volume) producing a result (price movement) commensurate with it.
concept.intuition: A price level that the crowd actually had to trade through to break carries more information than one that slipped away in a thin book.
concept.mechanics: Volume on the signal bar or swing is compared with a recent average and with prior comparable moves; confirmation is present when volume expands in the direction of the move and contracts on counter-moves or pullbacks.
concept.failure_modes: Volume is only fully known after the bar completes, so demanding confirmation structurally lags the move. Expiration, rebalance, or auction-imbalance volume can fabricate apparent confirmation.
concept.misconceptions: Confirmed moves still fail regularly; volume confirmation raises the information content of a move but does not certify continuation or improve reward-to-risk by itself.
concept.example: Price clears a resistance shelf and the breakout bar prints the session's highest volume with follow-through on the next bar; the same breakout on the session's lowest volume would be treated as unconfirmed.
